title: Realme raises phone prices by up to ₹5,000 at the start of festive buying
body: Realme raised prices on seven variants across three models by ₹1,000 to ₹5,000, effective October 12. The realme 16 5G (8GB+128GB) went from ₹36,999 to ₹41,999, a rise of about 13.5%. The company told retail partners the increases came from higher memory, chip and supply-chain costs. Kailash Lakhyani of retailer body AIMRA said 'Such counterproductive management decisions right at the start of festive buying will alienate consumers'. He added that buyers could switch to Samsung, Xiaomi, vivo or OPPO.

title: Samsung quietly adds ₹2,000 to Galaxy A27, M47 and F70 Pro prices
body: A leaked internal document shows Samsung applying a flat ₹2,000 increase across all storage variants of three phones, effective October 11. The Galaxy A27 6GB+128GB moved from ₹33,999 to ₹35,999, and the M47/F70 Pro 6GB+128GB moved from ₹35,999 to ₹37,999. Amazon, Flipkart and some physical stores were still showing the older prices during their festive promotions. The article reports no consumer reactions, and the figures come from a tipster's leak rather than a Samsung announcement.

title: Diwali 2026 costs more: appliances up to 7%, mithai up to 15%, pistachios nearly double
body: Appliance makers such as Haier, LG and Blue Star raised prices about 3% to 7%. A Delhi sweet chain reportedly raised prices by nearly 15%, and Tyohaar Sweets raised them 10% to 12%. Pistachios now sell at ₹1,500 to ₹2,100/kg against roughly ₹900/kg last Diwali, and almonds are up about 35%. Tyohaar's owner said she is using seed mixes instead of some dry fruits in gift hampers. Vijay Sales said about 70% of its purchases are made through EMIs, and Cellecor's Ravi Agarwal said buyers are 'researching products more carefully'.

title: Diwali airfares: 54% of festive flyers paid over 50% more, and a court told a petitioner 'Don't travel by air'
body: A plea alleged a 700% surge in Diwali airfares. A LocalCircles survey found 54% of festive travellers paid over 50% more than for comparable 2025 journeys. Aviation turbine fuel rose from about ₹60.50 per litre in March to ₹142 in May. Justice Vikram Nath declined an urgent hearing, saying 'Don't travel by air. Next case.' Social media users criticised the remark for ignoring steep fares, and the article notes that permanent fare controls still have not been introduced.

title: Nandini milk up ₹8 a litre from November 1; toned milk goes from ₹46 to ₹54
body: Karnataka's Cabinet approved the hike on October 29, effective November 1. Of the ₹8, ₹7 goes to farmers, raising their procurement price from ₹35 to ₹42 per litre. Farmers had asked for ₹10. Minister Krishna Byre Gowda compared milk to fuel, asking why a one-litre milk increase draws more debate than diesel and petrol reaching ₹100. Chief Minister DK Shivakumar said it was needed to prevent farmer losses amid higher transport, fuel and packaging costs. The Bengaluru Hotel Owners' Association called the rise 'unprecedented' and said a ₹2 to ₹3 increase would not have forced menu changes.

title: Bengaluru's tea and coffee get ₹3-₹5 costlier after the milk hike; ₹25 cup tests regulars
body: After milk rose ₹8 and curd ₹14, Bengaluru eateries raised tea and coffee by ₹3 to ₹5, with some coffee moving from ₹20 to ₹25. Petty shops raised tea and coffee by ₹5. Association president PC Rao said customers are absorbing the pass-through and warned ghee, butter, paneer and cheese may get pricier. A theatre artist said he and colleagues now share single cups. A technology worker said ₹25 no longer seems worth it for ordinary coffee, and an engineering student said the extra ₹5 adds up during exams.

title: Urban festive spending to fall 6% to ₹1.97 lakh crore as households dip into savings
body: The LocalCircles Mood of the Consumer 2026 survey covered over 67,000 urban household responses across 307 districts. It projects spending of ₹1.97 lakh crore, down 6% from ₹2.10 lakh crore in 2025. The average planned budget is nearly ₹20,000 per household. About 83% of planning households expect to use savings for part of their purchases, and 16% plan to fund them entirely from savings. September retail inflation was 5.54% and food inflation 7.74%. LocalCircles described 'a more subdued festive season'.

title: Dhanteras: gold ₹1,48,800 per 10g, down 19% from January peak; buyers go lighter and smaller
body: Delhi 24K gold was ₹1,48,800 per 10g, against a record ₹1,83,000 on January 29 and ₹1,32,400 last Dhanteras. Silver was ₹1,94,500 per kg, down 52% from its January peak of ₹4,04,500. Jewellers expect value growth of 20-30% but roughly flat volumes. Senco Gold said buyers are experimenting with designs and carats, and silver is drawing younger buyers. Kama Jewelry cautioned that demand is shifting to lightweight studded pieces and expects volumes down about 10%. The article notes the market slowed over six months amid rising prices and a government appeal against buying gold.

title: Maharashtra restaurants to raise menu prices 10-15% after Diwali
body: Restaurants across Maharashtra plan increases of 10-15% within about 8-10 days. An ₹80 idli could become roughly ₹88-92, and a ₹90 sada dosa roughly ₹99-104. Cited drivers include vegetables, grains, pulses, edible oil, commercial LPG, rent and staff costs. Pune restaurant association head Saili Jahagirdar said 'Raw materials are not just shooting up, they are shooting up exponentially'. The article warns final bills may rise even where menu changes look small, since each restaurant sets its own prices. Food inflation was 7.74% in September.

title: Commercial LPG up again on November 1, third straight rise, adding to eatery and hotel costs
body: The 19-kg commercial cylinder rose ₹10 to ₹2,820 in Delhi, from ₹2,810 on October 1, when it had risen ₹65. The article says the rise could add to operating costs for restaurants, hotels and caterers during the festive season. It attributes the movement to shipping disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz, higher freight and insurance costs, and crude oil prices. The page carries no quotes from businesses or consumers. It is relevant to the menu price rises in Bengaluru and Maharashtra.

title: iPhone 17 Diwali deals: ₹99,900 list price, Amazon vs Flipkart bank-offer maths
body: The iPhone 17 256GB lists at ₹99,900 on both platforms. Amazon sells it at ₹92,900 after a 7% discount, or ₹90,113 with Amazon Pay ICICI cashback. Flipkart sells it at ₹97,300 after 3% off, or ₹90,400 with an HDFC, ICICI or SBI card. Exchanging a Galaxy S25 5G on Flipkart with card offers brings it to ₹60,850. The article calls Amazon better without bank offers and Flipkart better for card holders and exchangers. It carries no reader reactions, and the real price depends on cards and exchange value.

title: ₹5 and ₹10 packs shrink or vanish as FMCG brands cut grammage
body: NielsenIQ's Q2 2026 data shows the share of ₹5 and ₹10 'magic price point' packs declining. A smaller Maggi pack that cost ₹10 years ago now sells for ₹12-15, and Frooti's ₹3 pack has largely disappeared. A ₹5 chips pack's quantity fell from about 17 g to 8 g in some cases, and Britannia plans 1.5-2% price adjustments mainly through grammage cuts. FIFI's Amit Lohani said below about 20 g 'consumers feel cheated' and expects a move from ₹5 to ₹10 packs. BCG's Nishant Shekhar said margins on these packs 'will continue to remain challenging'.

title: ServiceNow launches another round of layoffs hitting India, UK and US
body: ServiceNow began another global layoff round that reaches staff in India, the UK and the US, and has not said how many roles are going. Severance costs were $87 million in Q3 2026, up from $24 million a year earlier, and $167 million for the first nine months. The company says AI efficiencies generate more than $1 billion in annualised gains. CEO Bill McDermott called a smaller workforce a "gorgeous situation" on the earnings call, and the CFO tied slower hiring to AI productivity. The page carries no employee reactions.

title: Innodata lays off nearly 550 employees in India, staff lose system access before notice
body: Nearly 550 employees at Innodata's India operations were reportedly laid off on October 26, 2026, and the company has not confirmed the figure. Staff logged in and marked attendance as usual, then lost access to laptops, email and internal systems during the workday. Termination emails reportedly went to personal addresses and cited a "reduction in the business assignment". Affected workers set up WhatsApp groups to find out how many colleagues were hit. They were unsure about pending salaries and final settlements.

title: IT hiring splits in Q2: HCLTech adds 6,450 while Wipro sheds 6,716
body: In the September quarter, HCLTech's headcount rose to 230,339, including 6,136 fresher hires against 1,056 the quarter before. Infosys added 4,480 (332,542 total) and TCS rose to 598,056 from 593,798. Wipro fell by 6,716, about 2.8%, to 236,328. Attrition was 13.3% at TCS, 12.7% at Infosys voluntary and 13.8% at Wipro voluntary. TCS's HR head called its attrition "stable", and the page notes that attrition definitions differ across firms.

title: Qualcomm to begin global job cuts in November, number of roles unclear
body: Reuters, citing a memo from CEO Cristiano Amon, reports Qualcomm will start global job cuts in November 2026. The company had about 52,000 employees as of September 2025. Amon said the cuts will not rely only on individual performance, citing changing skill requirements and business priorities. The page does not say whether India staff are affected and carries no employee reactions.

title: H-1B worker laid off while visiting India, unsure if he can return to the US
body: An Indian professional on an H-1B visa was laid off while in India. The employer gave a day's notice, revoked his system access and set December 8, 2026 as his separation date. He shared the story on Reddit, where commenters disagreed on how employers notify US authorities. He is job hunting, which he calls challenging, and weighing a B-1/B-2 visa. USCIS allows a discretionary grace period of up to 60 days.

title: White-collar hiring up 14% in October, but Naukri flags a weak base
body: The Naukri JobSpeak index was 2,836 against 2,480 in October 2025, up 14%. Auto rose 36%, AI/ML 32% and GCCs 18%, while education fell 16%. Hiring for 0-3 years' experience rose 15%. Info Edge CEO Hitesh Oberoi said, "Some of October's growth reflects last year's festive-season base and we should read it in that light."

title: Indians want AI at work but not making every decision: Michael Page survey
body: Michael Page's Candidate Pulse Report 2026 surveyed 2,550 Indian respondents. 97% are willing to develop AI skills and 76% use interactive AI tools often or very often. 88% expect AI to improve productivity, but 65% worry about losing human judgment and 61% flag privacy and data security. Michael Page's Nilay Khandelwal said, "These safeguards have to be built into the ecosystem; otherwise, the trust factor will go away."

title: Infosys, TCS, Cognizant sharply cut H-1B registrations for FY2027
body: A Congressional Research Service report from October 14 shows Infosys registrations fell from 8,886 to 759, TCS from 5,955 to 284, and Cognizant from 3,752 to 0. A September federal proclamation put the combined drop for major firms at 24,946 to 2,055. The page says the report does not establish that any single policy caused the decline, and registrations are not hires. It carries no reactions.

title: Over 12,000 Indian tech professionals have left the US amid H-1B uncertainty and layoffs
body: The page says more than 12,000 Indian tech professionals have left the US. It also says Meta has cut about 8,000 jobs and Layoffs.fyi counted more than 110,000 cuts at 144 tech companies in 2026. Laid-off workers have up to 60 days to find a sponsor, change status or leave. Cato Institute figures cited say about 63% of pending green-card cases are Indian, with waits of 10 to 15 years. The page shows no reader comments.

title: Aon: salaries to rise 9.1% in 2027, attrition climbs to 18%
body: Aon's survey projects 9.1% salary increases for 2027 against 9% in 2026. Attrition rose to 18% from 16.2%, and involuntary attrition rose to 4% from 3.4%. 62% of companies are budgeting above 9%, and adoption of AI productivity tools is 56%, up from 46.1%. 42.8% of employers expect payroll costs to rise by at least 1% under the new wage code. Aon's Roopank Chaudhary pointed to "strong domestic consumption, sustained investment and export growth".

title: Microsoft offers voluntary exit to about 60,000 staff, including in India
body: Microsoft announced a voluntary exit offer covering India, the US, the UK and Canada, with about 60,000 employees eligible globally. It has about 23,000 employees in India, and it is unclear how many are eligible. Indian staff have until December 1 to decide, and the package is one month's base salary per completed year of service. Chief People Officer Amy Coleman called the offer "new for us" and said, "We'll learn from it". The page has no employee reactions.

title: IT services firms projected to see lowest salary hikes at 6.6% in 2027: Aon
body: Aon's 33rd India survey (1,200+ organisations, 45 industries) projects technology consulting and services at 6.6% for 2027, the lowest of the sectors listed and unchanged from 2026. NBFCs lead at 10.1%, followed by energy at 9.9%, GCCs at 9.4% and banking at 8.5%. Pay premiums for AI, machine learning and data science roles are up about 10% from 2025, and about 60% of employers are prioritising upskilling. The page notes 9.1% is an average, not a guarantee for every employee.

title: Chandigarh woman's workplace Diwali dance splits viewers on office professionalism
body: A woman from Chandigarh danced in traditional dress to 'Jhalla Wallah' at her office Diwali party while colleagues cheered. The page says the clip drew close to 20 million views across platforms. Some viewers loved the festive spirit. Others asked whether dancing at work is professional, and one quoted comment asked 'Aren't they embarrassed to do this at the workplace?' A recurring complaint was that it looked like entertaining foreign colleagues or clients. Defenders said it is a cultural celebration that builds team spirit.

title: Pilot's 'Diwali from above' Chennai reel crosses 7.5 million views
body: Pilot Pradeep Krishnan posted an Instagram clip of Chennai lit up for Diwali, captioned 'POV: Diwali from above.' The article says it had crossed 7.5 million views. He later clarified that the final frame was shot from the ground using 8x zoom, not from the cockpit. Commenters praised the view and posted festive wishes. One joked that only London rivals Chennai's Diwali glow.

title: Instagram tests 90-minute 'Features' videos to take on YouTube; Indian creators told not to assume access
body: Instagram is testing a 'Features' format that lets selected creators upload horizontal videos of up to 90 minutes. It began in Brazil and is expanding to a small group in the US, and Indian creators shouldn't assume they have it yet. It is aimed at podcasts, interviews and comedy shows that usually live on YouTube. Adam Mosseri said, 'I have been against doing long-form video on Instagram.' A Meta spokesperson said it is 'too early to share a long-term monetization model.' The page notes that YouTube's Partner Programme gives creators 55% of net ad revenue, and advises Indian creators to test Instagram but keep YouTube as the main home for full-length videos.

title: 19-year-old 'Gen Z Baba' says some online comments on him 'crossed all limits'
body: Shashwat Acharya, a 19-year-old spiritual speaker from Vrindavan known online as 'Gen Z Baba,' went viral largely for his youthful looks. In an NDTV interview he said some comments on his posts made him feel 'molested,' including remarks on his appearance such as his 'lotus eyes.' He added that comments passed on girls walking on the road are 'not even one per cent' of this. Many users flooded his posts with compliments, while others joked about suddenly taking an interest in spirituality. The story raises a question about the thirst-comment culture online.

title: Bengaluru PVR INOX juice counter shut after Instagram video shows reused disposable cups
body: A user posted an Instagram video on November 5 that allegedly showed staff at a PVR INOX juice counter in Forum Mall, South Bengaluru washing and reusing disposable cups. Karnataka food safety officers inspected it, found violations, issued a notice and closed the counter. Health Minister UT Khader said food safety rules apply equally to big brands and small vendors. Forum South Bengaluru apologised. Social media users questioned the multiplex's serving standards and asked for an explanation. It is another example of an ordinary customer's phone video prompting official action within a day.

title: Noida office's elderly staff member steals the show at Diwali party
body: An elderly staff member at a Noida company danced to 'Ishq Tera Tadpaave' at the office Diwali celebration while colleagues gathered, clapped and cheered. Employee Ishika Sahu filmed it and called him the uncle who stole the show. Social media users praised his cheerful spirit. Some urged employers to appreciate and reward hardworking support staff, and one suggested the company give him a gift. A colleague said they often see him in the lift and described him as a gentleman.

title: Deepinder Goyal defends Rs 85,000 Temple wearable as online criticism grows; Shubman Gill sighting sparks memes
body: Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal answered criticism of the Rs 85,000 Temple wearable in a post on X. He said it was built for a global market, expects no more than 1% of sales from India, and is 'strictly a fitness + AI device' that doesn't diagnose disease. He said 'Nobody is forcing you to buy' and told people not to back it just because it's Indian. Medical professionals questioned the science behind its brain blood-flow claims. A Free Press Journal piece dated 2026-11-04 says fans joked about Shubman Gill wearing the device and a red shirt, calling him a 'delivery partner,' and one user compared the device to a leech.

title: Ramayana makers warn against filming and sharing the film from cinemas
body: The makers of Ramayana (released November 5, 2026) said clips recorded inside theatres are circulating on social media and messaging apps. They cited Bombay High Court orders dated 2 November 2026 and 6 November 2026, and warned of criminal, civil and contempt action. They also said offenders would be reported to platforms, and told people to delete what they have posted. The page quotes no audience reaction. The warning shows the habit of filming big-screen moments for reels colliding with copyright enforcement.

title: Ramayana's Rs 4,000 crore budget compared with Chandrayaan-3 missions
body: Business Today compared the reported Rs 4,000 crore budget for the two Ramayana films with public projects. It works out to about 6.5 Chandrayaan-3 missions (Rs 615 crore) and about 8.9 Mars Orbiter Missions (about Rs 450 crore). At an average Day 1 advance ticket price of Rs 357, the budget equals about 11.2 crore tickets before taxes and cinema share. The page reports no public reactions, and it cautions that the comparisons only show scale. This kind of budget comparison is easy to share and argue over online.

title: Man fires fireworks from moving car on Dwarka Expressway; viewers call it reckless
body: A video that allegedly shows a man firing firecrackers from a moving car on Gurgaon's Dwarka Expressway circulated on X during Diwali. X users called it 'pure stupidity' that puts innocent lives at risk and said no stunt is worth it. One wrote that a few moments of showing off can outweigh a whole life. The article says the clip renewed calls for stricter festival traffic enforcement, and it reports no police response or figures.

title: Viral video of SpiceJet passengers allegedly abusing staff after cancellation at Bengaluru airport
body: A SpiceJet flight at Bengaluru airport was reportedly cancelled 30 minutes before departure on November 5, leaving more than 35 passengers allegedly stranded. A viral video shows a heated argument, and a woman passenger is accused of abusing staff and CISF personnel. The article says the details are not independently confirmed. Social media users criticised the passenger, saying frontline staff don't control cancellations and aren't the company's owners. The thread is about how people treat front-line workers when travel plans fail.

title: Swara Bhasker's 'Moti' blouse on Rise and Fall 2 draws attention to body-shaming of new mothers
body: DNA lists five viral moments from the Virender Sehwag-hosted show Rise and Fall 2. In the premiere, Swara Bhasker wore a blouse with the word 'Moti' to answer trolling about her post-partum weight. The list also covers a physical fight between contestants Siwet Tomar and Shehzad Poonawalla, and her account of two failed IVF cycles. The page gives no ratings or viewership figures and quotes no viewers. It says viewers speculated about which cricketers messaged contestant Sara Gurpal, and that the blouse gesture drew attention to how public figures are scrutinised over their looks after motherhood.

title: Suriya's Scene holds up on Day 2 as occupancy climbs
body: Suriya's Tamil-Telugu film Scene took ₹20.35 Cr net on its second day (Saturday), against ₹19.15 Cr on Day 1. That is a 6.3% rise, and the page is stamped as published Nov 7 and updated Nov 8. India net after two days was ₹39.50 Cr, and worldwide gross was ₹79.65 Cr. Shows fell from 6,167 to 5,687, but occupancy rose from 55.0% to 62.5%, which the article reads as people actually turning up. Tamil made up about 81% of Day 2 net, and night shows for the Tamil 2D version were fullest at 83.7%. The figures are Sacnilk estimates, and the page has no direct audience quotes.

title: Ramayana: Part One gets 'super positive' audience scores on opening day
body: Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana opened on Diwali week with strong audience scores. BookMyShow shows 9.4/10 from 48.2K+ votes, Sacnilk audience 9.5/10 from 238 ratings, and IMDb 8.7/10 from 8.9K ratings. Rotten Tomatoes audience is 93% from 50+ ratings, while critics are at 75% from 32 reviews. The article says viewers praised the visual scale, the performances and the emotional moments. Critics were more measured, with some raising concerns about pacing and storytelling. The page says these early scores could still change.

title: Ramayana's Rahman–Zimmer score splits listeners after release
body: Ramayana is the first Indian film score for Hans Zimmer, who worked with A.R. Rahman. Even after release, reactions stayed divided. Some listeners felt the score lacked emotional depth and sounded more like Hollywood spectacle than a devotional story. Others praised it in action scenes, and the Jatayu sequence was named as a clear success. 'Ravana Tandav' was debated before release but gained appreciation on screen. The article says 'Mangal Rang' reached the top of YouTube's trending music chart. Rahman is quoted saying the workload equalled roughly ten films.

title: Rahman's 'Mangal Rang' from Ramayana sparks qawwali debate
body: The wedding song 'Mangal Rang' came out on October 25 and started an argument online. Some listeners questioned whether qawwali and Sufi-style sounds suit a screen retelling of a Hindu epic. Others defended Rahman's freedom to experiment, and some compared it to 'Kun Faya Kun' from Rockstar. Rahman told Hindustan Times he focuses on the creative process rather than online feedback. The page gives worldwide bookings of about Rs205 million as of October 26, per Sacnilk. The page shows only a 'last updated' date of October 26.

title: Jailer 2 opens huge in Kerala, but Mohanlal fans are angry
body: Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 earned ₹12.50 crore gross in Kerala on Day 1. That is the second-highest opening day in the state, behind Empuraan (₹14 crore) and ahead of Leo (₹12 crore). Nationally, Day 1 was ₹70.25 crore India gross and ₹125.25 crore worldwide gross, with ₹59.70 crore domestic net, per Sacnilk. Many Mohanlal fans were disappointed that his role was cut. His costume designer said three looks were dropped and that he won't work on a Jailer 3. Fans online accused the makers of trimming Mohanlal to keep the focus on Rajinikanth.

title: Shah Rukh Khan's 'Tu Mil Jaaye' from King becomes most-watched Indian film song in 24 hours
body: The song from King, with Deepika Padukone, was released on November 2 for Shah Rukh Khan's 61st birthday. It got 36.3 million YouTube views in 24 hours, ahead of 'Zinda Banda' from Jawan at 34.6 million. It also had over 430,000 YouTube likes and more than 60 million views across all platforms in a day. The article calls the response from his fans overwhelming. It does not quote any fans or social media posts.

title: Netflix's Akka gets mixed-to-negative reviews on release day
body: YRF's gangster series Akka, with Keerthy Suresh and Radhika Apte, streamed worldwide on October 30 with five episodes of 30 to 46 minutes. Early reviews lean negative. The Tribune gave it 2.5 stars and Free Press Journal gave it 2 stars, and critics praised the leads but faulted the script. The Federal said it falls short of its premise and reported that it was finished in 2024 and reshot several times. IWM Buzz was the most positive, calling it engaging and well shot. The page has no audience numbers. An OTT chart snippet from my earlier search listed Akka among the top trending titles.

title: Bigg Boss Telugu 10 accused of losing family viewers over pool scene
body: A recent Bigg Boss Telugu season 10 episode showed anchor Varshini getting close to Mukesh in the swimming pool, and the article says it did not go over well with viewers. Commenters said the house feels like a show rather than a home. One post said the captains' group was favoured over Mukesh's group, and another accused the show of favouring Varshini. The article reports that neither Bigg Boss nor host Nagarjuna questioned the two. It gives no ratings figures. The reactions come from a handful of social media posts dated October 8–9, not measured viewership.

title: Mookuthi Amman 2 lands as a Diwali release with a middling 2.5/5 review
body: DT Next gave Nayanthara's devotional film 2.5/5 in a review updated November 6. It praised Nayanthara, Urvashi, Hip Hop Tamizha Aadhi's music and the editing. It faulted the film for little humour, a weak emotional pull and heavy dependence on VFX and AI imagery. The page has no audience reactions. A related Sacnilk page lists ₹4.33 crore earned in November so far, with no cumulative total. Other reviews I saw, from Hollywood Reporter India and Flick on Click, were also lukewarm, though I did not open them.

title: Godzilla Minus Zero pushed to November 20 in India to make room for Ramayana
body: Godzilla Minus Zero's India release moved from November 6 to November 20 after Ramayana took a reported two-week IMAX exclusivity window. The article says the Godzilla film, made for IMAX, could have got only a handful of premium shows if it had opened alongside Ramayana. At the time, Ramayana showed ₹182.70 Cr India net and ₹387.25 Cr worldwide gross. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping also opens November 20, so premium screens will be split three ways. The page has no audience reactions. The analysis is the writer's own, and Godzilla Minus One's earlier $116 million-plus gross is cited for context.

title: Final India–West Indies T20I washed out in Bengaluru, series ends 2-2
body: The fifth T20I at the Chinnaswamy Stadium started 1 hour 45 minutes late and was cut to nine overs a side. India reached 118-5 after 7.4 overs, including Naman Dhir's unbeaten 24 off six balls, before rain ended play after 48 minutes. The series finished 2-2. Ishan Kishan hit the series' 100th six, off Romario Shepherd. More than 20,000 fans turned up despite the weather. The page has no fan quotes. The result is a dead rubber that left the series level.

title: Gill's India face Kohli-Rohit questions: BCCI picks two ODI squads for New Zealand
body: The BCCI named separate squads for a five-ODI tour of New Zealand. Shubman Gill captains the first three ODIs from Auckland on November 4, and Shreyas Iyer leads the last two at Mount Maunganui on November 13 and 15. Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli are in both squads, Ravindra Jadeja is out of the ODIs, and Jasprit Bumrah is rested from the ODIs but in the Test squad. The page has no fan reactions. After the earlier West Indies ODIs, Gill said on October 4 that fielding and death bowling need work before the World Cup. The page shows an October 17 posted date and an 8 Nov footer.

title: Festive rush leaves gig workers with fewer jobs, flat pay
body: The Financial Express report, carried by IPA Newspack, says delivery partners and warehouse staff saw little extra pay this festive season. Horizontal e-commerce platforms hired 20-30% fewer seasonal workers than planned, and per-shipment payouts fell to Rs 12-15 from Rs 25-28 last year. Quick-commerce per-order payouts are Rs 20-30 plus Rs 8-15 in peak additions, against Rs 34-42 in early 2024. Demand for quick-commerce gig workers grew 18%, versus 12% in e-commerce. Shaik Salauddin of the Telangana Gig and Platform Workers' Union said: "When orders are uncertain, incentive targets become harder to meet, forcing riders to stay online longer."

title: Your train ticket could fall by ₹15 to ₹75 from January: here's why
body: More than 40 trains are reported to lose superfast status from 1 January 2027 because they miss the required average speed, which the article gives as 55 kmph. The list includes the Mahanagari, Pragati, Tulsi and Sapt Kranti trains. Surcharge savings per passenger are ₹15 (second class), ₹30 (sleeper), ₹45 (AC chair car, 3-tier and 2-tier) and ₹75 (AC first class). A family of four in sleeper would save ₹120 per trip. The article says no zone has published a revised fare table or clarified refunds for surcharges already paid. It also says the Central and East Central Railway notices could not be found on railway websites.

title: 50% work from home in Delhi-NCR till 20 November: who's covered and who isn't
body: The Commission for Air Quality Management issued an order on 30 October. From 5 to 20 November, state and private offices in Delhi and five NCR districts can have no more than 50% of staff on site. Industrial units and essential services are exempt where remote work isn't feasible. Delhi's AQI reached 377 by 4 November, and GRAP Stage II has been active since 2 November. The article reports no reactions from employees or companies. It describes the order as "preventive", based on a review of November data from 2018 to 2025.

title: How much cash can you keep at home? The limits that actually matter
body: This explainer says India has no legal cap on cash held at home, but you must be able to explain where it came from. Under the new Income-tax Act, 2025, receiving ₹2 lakh or more in cash from one person in a day is restricted, and taking a cash loan or deposit of ₹20,000 or more is barred. The special tax on unexplained cash is now 30%, about 39% with surcharge and cess, against about 78% earlier. Misreporting penalties can reach 200% of the tax. The article cites CA Club India and advises keeping bank slips, sale deeds and gift records. It quotes no public reaction.

title: How much gold can you keep at home? The 500g rule explained
body: With gold prices high, the article explains the tax-search limits for family jewellery: 500g for a married woman, 250g for an unmarried woman and 100g for a male family member. In its example family, the total is 950g. At Upstox's 3 November rate of ₹13,812 per gram, that is worth about ₹1.31 crore. The special tax rate on unexplained assets is reportedly cut from 60% to 30% from 1 April 2026. Long-term capital gains on gold are taxed at 12.5% after more than 24 months. The page reports no public reactions.

title: How much gold can you bring from Dubai? 40g for women, 20g for others
body: A woman returning after more than a year abroad can bring 40g of gold jewellery duty-free, and others can bring 20g. Gold import duty was raised from 6% to 15% on 13 May 2026. On 5 November, Dubai 22K gold was about ₹1,18,577 per 10g against ₹1,31,060 in Delhi, a gap of about ₹12,483 per 10g. The article's worked example puts the extra duty on 10g at about ₹17,787. It warns that undeclared gold can lead to confiscation and prosecution. It reports no traveller reactions.

title: Why petrol is ₹117.51 in Andhra Pradesh and ₹88.66 in Andaman
body: Petrol costs ₹117.51 per litre in Andhra Pradesh and ₹88.66 in Andaman and Nicobar, a gap of ₹28.85, mostly because of state taxes. A 40-litre tank costs about ₹4,085 in Delhi and about ₹4,700 in Andhra Pradesh. Delhi petrol has stayed at ₹102.12 since four hikes in May. Brent crude settled at $94.62 on 4 November, down nearly 20% for the week, but no pump price cut has been announced. HDFC Sky is quoted as saying the crude drop may not last.

title: Diwali crackers in Delhi-NCR: the time slots, QR check and 300-metre rule
body: The Supreme Court allowed certified green crackers in Delhi-NCR only on 7 and 8 November, in the windows 6-7 am and 8-10 pm, and the full ban returns on 9 November. Each sealed box needs a QR code, and online sales are banned. No crackers may be used within 300 metres of hospitals and schools. Outlook, citing Hindustan Times spot checks, reported that vendors in Sadar Bazaar and Chandni Chowk were selling crackers and many boxes lacked QR codes. Justice Sundresh remarked that "now everything is available."

title: Hyderabad-Patna flights cut by half before Chhath: what travellers should know
body: Airlines have cut flights to and from Patna ahead of Chhath (13-16 November). Patna has 302 weekly departures this month, down from 377 in October 2025, and Hyderabad-Patna fell from 90 weekly flights to 42, a 53% cut. Delhi-Patna fares reportedly reached nearly three times the usual ₹6,000-8,000 on some dates. Business Standard attributes the cuts to high fares, fuel costs, a weaker rupee and softer demand. The article points travellers to special train 03294 and Vande Bharat specials. It warns that unconfirmed waitlisted e-tickets cannot be boarded.

title: Economist Shamika Ravi on why Indians remain obsessed with sarkari jobs
body: Economist Shamika Ravi of the PM's Economic Advisory Council said the pull of government jobs is about status: "It's a matter of prestige; it's a matter of power." She linked it to India's feudal past. She cited a Tamil Nadu study in the Journal of Public Economics finding that people who never sat government exams had higher lifetime earnings than comparable people who spent years preparing. She argued that five to seven years of exam prep in one's 20s means lost work experience. The unemployment rates she quoted were around 3% for all-India, 0.9% for Gujarat, 1.2% for Karnataka and 12% for Kerala.

title: 60 per cent Gen Z shoppers spend more on festive shopping, study finds
body: A YouGov and Rukam Capital study of 4,002 people aged 18-29 found that 60% spent more during major festivals and 40% made unplanned purchases. Family pressure was the top driver of overspending at 34%, ahead of discounts (29%) and emotional connections (28%). Clothing and food were each at 49% of spending, and 74% bought gifts for parents and relatives. For gift ideas, online search (41%) edged out personal judgement (39%), and 25% used AI tools. The article says family expectations played the biggest role when young shoppers went beyond their budgets.

title: 71% of Gen Z prefer celebrating Diwali traditionally, but 66% want more fun: Sanrio survey
body: This Sanrio-commissioned survey found 71% of Gen Z say Diwali is best celebrated the traditional way, while 66% want more playfulness. 64% prefer gifts that show they understand the recipient's habits, and 60% value personal meaning over gifts meant to impress on social media. 60% prefer smaller gatherings, and spending time together (57%) was the top way to feel connected. By city, 68% in Hyderabad plan to spend time with family, against 53-57% elsewhere. In Delhi NCR, 47% strongly agree on celebrating traditionally, against 34% in Hyderabad. The page is brand-commissioned, so it reflects the survey's framing.
